matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When relocating a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal). Rotating a stick to a different orientation creates an illegal shape and invalidates the character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Anytime you consider moving a stick, first check its orientation and keep it unchanged.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick from a V and placing it as a horizontal stick to form a minus sign.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere. The total number of sticks in the whole equation stays constant.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of planning a move, ensure you are only relocating a single existing stick.
matchstick.example: Adding a new vertical stick to an I to make an L without removing any stick from another character.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =). Any shape that does not correspond to one of these symbols makes the whole equation invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a change, scan each character to confirm it matches a permitted symbol.
matchstick.example: Turning a V into a shape with three diagonal sticks, which is not a recognized Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and check that the equality holds after the stick move. A visually correct arrangement is useless if the arithmetic is wrong.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate corrected equation, perform the numeric check before finalising the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting "XV = XV + XV" without noticing that 15 ≠ 30.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonals and remain a valid X or V. Removing a diagonal from either numeral leaves an invalid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before taking a diagonal from an X or V, verify that the source will still have two diagonals.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from a V, leaving a single diagonal line that is not a Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved to a different position inside the same numeral, altering its shape while keeping the character valid (e.g., reposition a diagonal within V to turn it into X). This counts as a single‑stick move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single stick can change a numeral’s shape without affecting any other character.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal inside a V to a new crossing position but leaving the V with only one diagonal, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved from one character to a different character, altering both; ensure that after the move both source and destination remain legal symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the solution requires moving a stick between distinct characters (e.g., from an I to the minus sign).
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from an I to the minus sign, leaving the I empty and the minus sign without a horizontal bar.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching "Correct version of the equation: <equation>", using uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace. Any deviation causes the answer to be rejected.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Just before submitting the final answer.
matchstick.example: Omitting the required prefix or using lowercase letters, resulting in a format mismatch.

matchstick.title: Validate single‑stick relocation feasibility
matchstick.principle: After proposing a corrected equation, verify that the change from the original can be achieved by moving exactly one stick. You must not have altered multiple sticks or characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate equation, compare it to the original to ensure only one stick changed.
matchstick.example: Changing "VI" to "XI" by adding a diagonal and removing a vertical, which requires two separate sticks.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: I consists of a single vertical stick; you cannot move that stick away without replacing it, because the source would become empty and invalid. Only move a vertical from an I if the I is part of a larger group (e.g., "II") that can remain valid after removal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before moving a vertical stick from an I, check whether the source numeral will still be a legal Roman numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving the only vertical stick from a solitary I, leaving no character at that position.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual transformation and forgets to check the numeric values of the resulting Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers after a proposed change and confirm the equality holds.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model generates the corrected equation but omits or miswrites the required final line, causing the parser to miss the answer.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: End the response with exactly "Correct version of the equation: <equation>" using uppercase letters and single spaces.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character without placing it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that every moved stick must be placed on a destination character; never leave a gap.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away (including I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a crucial stick from a numeral, leaving it in an invalid shape (e.g., turning I into nothing or X/V into a single diagonal).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that the source numeral remains a legal Roman numeral after the stick is removed.

matchstick.description: Proposed equation not reachable by a single stick move (multiple sticks changed)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes several characters simultaneously, which would require moving more than one stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compare the original and candidate equations character‑by‑character to ensure only one stick has been relocated.
